subject: math
title: Picture Graphs and Bar Graphs
seo_title: Grade 3 Picture Graphs and Bar Graphs Worksheets: Scaled Graphs, How Many More and Two-Step Questions
standard_text: Draw a scaled picture graph and a scaled bar graph to represent a data set with several categories. Solve one- and two-step “how many more” and “how many less” problems using information presented in scaled bar graphs.
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 picture graph and bar graph worksheets: read scaled graphs with a key, half pictures and bars between grid lines, solve how many more and how many fewer questions, two-step problems, and draw your own graphs. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Check the key or the scale first. Then read the graph.
key_sub: Each picture or grid space can stand for 2, 5, 10 or more. Multiply the pictures by the key, and read bars against the scale. How many more or fewer means subtract.
body_html:
What a scaled graph is

A graph shows data so you can compare it at a glance. In a scaled graph, one picture or one grid space can stand for more than 1. The key or the scale tells you how much.

Read a picture graph

Look at the key first. Then count the pictures in a row and multiply by the key. Half a picture stands for half of the key.

Example

How many votes did Grape get?

Grape has 5 circles. 5 × 2 = 10.

Answer: 10 votes

Read a bar graph

Find what the scale counts by: 2, 5, 10 or another number. Follow the top of the bar across to the scale. If a bar ends halfway between two lines, the value is halfway between the two numbers.

How many more? How many fewer?

Read both bars, then subtract the smaller number from the bigger number.

Example

Using the pet graph: how many more students have a dog than a bird?

Dog: 12. Bird: 9. 12 − 9 = 3.

Answer: 3 more students

Two-step questions

Some questions need two steps. Do the first step (often adding two bars), then answer the real question.

Example

How many more students have a dog or a cat than a bird?

Step 1: 12 + 7 = 19. Step 2: 19 − 9 = 10.

Answer: 10 more students

Draw your own scaled graph

Pick a scale that fits your biggest number. Then divide each number by the scale.

DataPicture graph (each star = 5)Bar graph (scale of 5)
Dog 357 starsbar ends at 35 (7 spaces)
Cat 204 starsbar ends at 20 (4 spaces)
Fish 153 starsbar ends at 15 (3 spaces)
Bird 255 starsbar ends at 25 (5 spaces)

Always give your graph a title, label both axes, and write the key or the scale.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting pictures instead of using the key (5 circles = 5)Multiply by the key: 5 × 2 = 10
Skipping a half pictureHalf a picture is half of the key
Counting grid spaces as 1 eachCheck what the scale counts by
Adding when the question says how many moreHow many more or fewer means subtract
Answering after one stepRead the question again: is there a second step?

faq.q: What is a scaled picture graph?
faq.a: It is a picture graph where each picture stands for more than one thing, such as each star = 5 votes. The key tells the value, so 4 stars mean 4 × 5 = 20 votes.

faq.q: How do you read a scaled bar graph in 3rd grade?
faq.a: First find what the scale counts by, such as 2, 5 or 10. Then follow the top of the bar across to the number on the scale. A bar that ends halfway between 10 and 20 shows 15.

faq.q: How do you solve how many more and how many fewer questions with a bar graph?
faq.a: Read the two bars, then subtract the smaller number from the bigger number. If Soccer has 25 votes and Tennis has 10, Soccer has 25 − 10 = 15 more votes.

faq.q: What does half a picture mean on a picture graph?
faq.a: Half a picture stands for half of the key. If each circle = 10 students, half a circle = 5 students, so 3 and a half circles = 35 students.

sets.title: Read a picture graph with a key

items.q: How many stickers does Lily have?
items.e: Each circle stands for 2 stickers. The Lily row has 2 circles and half a circle: 2 × 2 = 4, and half of 2 is 1, so 4 + 1 = 5 stickers.
Each star stands for 5 books. The Sports row has 3 stars: 3 × 5 = 15 books.

items.q: How many cans did Room 3 collect?
items.e: Each square stands for 10 cans. The Room 3 row has 4 squares and half a square: 4 × 10 = 40, and half of 10 is 5, so 40 + 5 = 45 cans.

items.q: How many votes did Pear get?
items.e: Each circle stands for 2 votes. The Pear row has 7 circles: 7 × 2 = 14 votes.
Each star stands for 10 votes. The Green row has 2 stars and half a star: 2 × 10 = 20, and half of 10 is 5, so 20 + 5 = 25 votes.

items.q: How many cups of lemonade were sold on Monday?

items.q: How many robins were seen?
items.e: Each circle stands for 2 birds. The Robin row has 5 circles and half a circle: 5 × 2 = 10, and half of 2 is 1, so 10 + 1 = 11 birds.
Each star stands for 10 students. The Hockey row has 4 stars: 4 × 10 = 40 students.

items.q: How many students chose pizza?

items.q: How many books did Maya read?

Each star stands for 5 cones. The Chocolate row has 2 stars: 2 × 5 = 10 cones.

items.q: How many points did the Tigers score?

items.q: How many days were cloudy?
items.e: Each circle stands for 2 days. The Cloudy row has 4 circles and half a circle: 4 × 2 = 8, and half of 2 is 1, so 8 + 1 = 9 days.
Every star has the same value, so the row with the most stars wins. The Oak row has 5 stars: 5 × 5 = 25 trees.

items.q: Which row shows the fewest students?
items.e: Every square has the same value, so the row with the fewest squares wins. The Walk row has 2 squares: 2 × 10 = 20 students.

items.q: Which row shows the most students?
items.e: Every circle has the same value, so the row with the most circles wins. The Dog row has 6 circles: 6 × 2 = 12 students.
The key says one whole star = 2 shells. Half a star is half of 2, which is 1 shell.

items.q: In this graph, what does half a square stand for?
items.e: The key says one whole square = 10 votes. Half a square is half of 10, which is 5 votes.

items.q: Which row shows 5 students?
items.e: 5 students ÷ 5 = 1, so look for a row with 1 circle. The Soccer row has 1 circle: 1 × 5 = 5 students.
30 votes ÷ 10 = 3, so look for a row with 3 stars. The Purple row has 3 stars: 3 × 10 = 30 votes.

sets.title: How many more? How many fewer?

items.q: How many more students have a cat than a hamster?
items.e: The scale counts by 2. The Cat bar ends at the line for 8. The Hamster bar ends halfway between 2 and 4, so it shows 3. 8 − 3 = 5, so the answer is 5 more students.

items.q: How many fewer votes did Fall get than Summer?
items.e: The scale counts by 5. The Summer bar ends at the line for 35. The Fall bar ends at the line for 20. 35 − 20 = 15, so the answer is 15 fewer votes.

items.q: How many more cups were sold on Monday than on Tuesday?
items.e: The Mon row has 5 squares: 5 × 10 = 50 cups. The Tue row has 1 square: 1 × 10 = 10 cups. 50 − 10 = 40, so the answer is 40 more cups.

items.q: How many fewer books did Leo read than Ben?
items.e: The scale counts by 2. The Ben bar ends halfway between 8 and 10, so it shows 9. The Leo bar ends halfway between 2 and 4, so it shows 3. 9 − 3 = 6, so the answer is 6 fewer books.

items.q: How many more chocolate cones than mint cones were sold?
items.e: The scale counts by 5. The Chocolate bar ends at the line for 35. The Mint bar ends at the line for 25. 35 − 25 = 10, so the answer is 10 more cones.

items.q: How many fewer students chose pizza than pasta?
items.e: The Pasta row has 4 squares: 4 × 10 = 40 students. The Pizza row has 2 squares: 2 × 10 = 20 students. 40 − 20 = 20, so the answer is 20 fewer students.

items.q: How many more students come by car to school than ride the bus?
items.e: The scale counts by 10. The Car bar ends halfway between 60 and 70, so it shows 65. The Bus bar ends at the line for 40. 65 − 40 = 25, so the answer is 25 more students.

items.q: How many fewer votes did Purple get than Red?
items.e: The scale counts by 2. The Red bar ends at the line for 14. The Purple bar ends at the line for 10. 14 − 10 = 4, so the answer is 4 fewer votes.

items.q: How many more shells did Sam find than Eli?
items.e: The Sam row has 4 squares: 4 × 5 = 20 shells. The Eli row has 3 squares: 3 × 5 = 15 shells. 20 − 15 = 5, so the answer is 5 more shells.

items.q: How many fewer stickers does Lily have than Ruby?
items.e: The scale counts by 10. The Ruby bar ends halfway between 30 and 40, so it shows 35. The Lily bar ends at the line for 10. 35 − 10 = 25, so the answer is 25 fewer stickers.

items.q: How many more days were rainy than windy?
items.e: The scale counts by 2. The Rainy bar ends at the line for 12. The Windy bar ends at the line for 2. 12 − 2 = 10, so the answer is 10 more days.

items.q: How many fewer votes did Grape get than Banana?
items.e: The scale counts by 5. The Banana bar ends at the line for 35. The Grape bar ends at the line for 30. 35 − 30 = 5, so the answer is 5 fewer votes.

items.q: How many more students chose swimming than baseball?
items.e: The Swimming row has 6 circles and half a circle: 6 × 10 = 60, and half of 10 is 5, so 60 + 5 = 65 students. The Baseball row has 1 circle and half a circle: 1 × 10 = 10, and half of 10 is 5, so 10 + 5 = 15 students. 65 − 15 = 50, so the answer is 50 more students.

items.q: How many fewer points did the Bears score than the Tigers?
items.e: The scale counts by 2. The Tigers bar ends at the line for 12. The Bears bar ends at the line for 10. 12 − 10 = 2, so the answer is 2 fewer points.

items.q: How many more votes did Grape get than Pear?
items.e: The scale counts by 5. The Grape bar ends at the line for 20. The Pear bar ends at the line for 10. 20 − 10 = 10, so the answer is 10 more votes.

items.q: How many fewer maple trees than oak trees are in the park?
items.e: The Oak row has 6 circles and half a circle: 6 × 10 = 60, and half of 10 is 5, so 60 + 5 = 65 trees. The Maple row has 2 circles and half a circle: 2 × 10 = 20, and half of 10 is 5, so 20 + 5 = 25 trees. 65 − 25 = 40, so the answer is 40 fewer trees.

items.q: How many more books did Ava read than Noah?
items.e: The scale counts by 2. The Ava bar ends at the line for 14. The Noah bar ends at the line for 4. 14 − 4 = 10, so the answer is 10 more books.

items.q: How many fewer Sports books than Animals books were checked out?
items.e: The scale counts by 10. The Animals bar ends at the line for 40. The Sports bar ends at the line for 20. 40 − 20 = 20, so the answer is 20 fewer books.

items.q: How many more votes did Red get than Green?
items.e: The Red row has 6 circles: 6 × 5 = 30 votes. The Green row has 3 circles: 3 × 5 = 15 votes. 30 − 15 = 15, so the answer is 15 more votes.

items.q: How many fewer students chose salad than tacos?
items.e: The scale counts by 2. The Tacos bar ends at the line for 10. The Salad bar ends at the line for 2. 10 − 2 = 8, so the answer is 8 fewer students.

items.q: How many students voted in all?
items.e: Step 1: read every bar: Tennis 3, Hockey 9, Baseball 7, Swimming 12. Step 2: add them: 3 + 9 + 7 + 12 = 31 students.

items.q: How many cones were sold in all?
items.e: Step 1: read every bar: Chocolate 10, Mint 35, Mango 15, Vanilla 30. Step 2: add them: 10 + 35 + 15 + 30 = 90 cones.

items.q: How many cups were sold in all?
items.e: Step 1: read every bar: Tue 20, Wed 40, Thu 45, Fri 30. Step 2: add them: 20 + 40 + 45 + 30 = 135 cups.

items.q: How many shells did they find in all?
items.e: Step 1: read every bar: Owen 20, Eli 5, Sam 30, Mia 15. Step 2: add them: 20 + 5 + 30 + 15 = 70 shells.

items.q: How many more stickers do the Grace and Kai bars show together than the Omar bar?
items.e: Step 1: Grace + Kai = 65 + 60 = 125. Step 2: compare with Omar (70): 125 − 70 = 55, so 55 more stickers.

items.q: How many more students do the Bird and Dog bars show together than the Cat bar?
items.e: Step 1: Bird + Dog = 10 + 12 = 22. Step 2: compare with Cat (14): 22 − 14 = 8, so 8 more students.

items.q: How many more birds do the Blue Jay and Finch bars show together than the Sparrow bar?
items.e: Step 1: Blue Jay + Finch = 15 + 30 = 45. Step 2: compare with Sparrow (35): 45 − 35 = 10, so 10 more birds.

items.q: How many more votes do the Fall and Winter bars show together than the Spring bar?
items.e: Step 1: Fall + Winter = 50 + 30 = 80. Step 2: compare with Spring (70): 80 − 70 = 10, so 10 more votes.

items.q: How many students did not choose soccer?
items.e: Step 1: add all the bars: 15 + 30 + 35 + 5 = 85. Step 2: take away Soccer (30): 85 − 30 = 55 students. Or add the other three bars: 15 + 35 + 5 = 55.

items.q: How many votes were not for Yellow?
items.e: Step 1: add all the bars: 60 + 70 + 20 + 10 = 160. Step 2: take away Yellow (70): 160 − 70 = 90 votes. Or add the other three bars: 60 + 20 + 10 = 90.

items.q: How many days were not windy?
items.e: Step 1: add all the bars: 8 + 13 + 5 + 4 = 30. Step 2: take away Windy (4): 30 − 4 = 26 days. Or add the other three bars: 8 + 13 + 5 = 26.

items.q: What is the difference between the greatest number and the least number of cans?
items.e: Step 1: find the greatest and the least. The Room 3 bar is the greatest (60). The Room 4 bar is the least (10). Step 2: 60 − 10 = 50 cans.

items.q: What is the difference between the greatest number and the least number of points?
items.e: Step 1: find the greatest and the least. The Lions bar is the greatest (35). The Tigers bar is the least (10). Step 2: 35 − 10 = 25 points.

items.q: What is the difference between the greatest number and the least number of shells?
items.e: Step 1: find the greatest and the least. The Mia bar is the greatest (14). The Eli bar is the least (2). Step 2: 14 − 2 = 12 shells.

items.q: How many more students do the Walk and Bus bars show together than the Bike and Car bars?
items.e: Step 1: Walk + Bus = 65 + 40 = 105, and Bike + Car = 50 + 45 = 95. Step 2: 105 − 95 = 10, so 10 more students.

items.q: How many more points do the Hawks and Lions bars show together than the Tigers and Bears bars?
items.e: Step 1: Hawks + Lions = 14 + 2 = 16, and Tigers + Bears = 6 + 4 = 10. Step 2: 16 − 10 = 6, so 6 more points.

items.q: How many more books do the Sports and Mystery bars show together than the Space and Animals bars?
items.e: Step 1: Sports + Mystery = 35 + 10 = 45, and Space + Animals = 25 + 15 = 40. Step 2: 45 − 40 = 5, so 5 more books.

items.q: How many students do the Pizza and Pasta rows show in all?
items.e: Step 1: The Pizza row has 2 squares: 2 × 2 = 4 students. The Pasta row has 1 square: 1 × 2 = 2 students. Step 2: 4 + 2 = 6 students.

items.q: How many votes do the Spring and Fall rows show in all?
items.e: Step 1: The Spring row has 2 circles and half a circle: 2 × 10 = 20, and half of 10 is 5, so 20 + 5 = 25 votes. The Fall row has 6 circles and half a circle: 6 × 10 = 60, and half of 10 is 5, so 60 + 5 = 65 votes. Step 2: 25 + 65 = 90 votes.
Step 1: The Hamster row has 6 stars: 6 × 2 = 12 students. The Fish row has 1 star: 1 × 2 = 2 students. Step 2: 12 + 2 = 14 students.

sets.title: Make graphs and solve word problems

items.q: The bar for Chocolate is missing. It should show 10 cones. How many grid spaces tall should the bar be?
items.e: Each grid space stands for 5. 10 ÷ 5 = 2, so the bar is 2 spaces tall and ends at the line for 10. Drawing 10 spaces would forget the scale.

items.q: The bar for Sparrow is missing. It should show 4 birds. How many grid spaces tall should the bar be?
items.e: Each grid space stands for 2. 4 ÷ 2 = 2, so the bar is 2 spaces tall and ends at the line for 4. Drawing 4 spaces would forget the scale.

items.q: The bar for Room 4 is missing. It should show 50 cans. How many grid spaces tall should the bar be?
items.e: Each grid space stands for 10. 50 ÷ 10 = 5, so the bar is 5 spaces tall and ends at the line for 50. Drawing 50 spaces would forget the scale.

items.q: The bar for Car is missing. It should show 35 students. Where should the top of the bar be?
items.e: The scale counts by 10. 35 is between 30 and 40, exactly in the middle (30 + 5 = 35). So the bar ends halfway between the two lines.

items.q: The bar for Ben is missing. It should show 5 books. Where should the top of the bar be?
items.e: The scale counts by 2. 5 is between 4 and 6, exactly in the middle (4 + 1 = 5). So the bar ends halfway between the two lines.

items.q: On a picture graph, each star stands for 5 books. Ava read 35 books. How many stars should be in Ava's row?
items.e: 35 ÷ 5 = 7, so draw 7 stars. Check: 7 × 5 = 35. Drawing 35 would forget the key.

items.q: On a picture graph, each circle stands for 2 points. The Tigers scored 9 points. How many circles should be in the Tigers' row?
items.e: 9 ÷ 2 = 4 with 1 left over. 1 is half of 2, so draw 4 circles and half a circle. Check: 4 × 2 + 1 = 9.

items.q: On a picture graph, each square stands for 10 cans. Room 3 collected 60 cans. How many squares should be in the Room 3 row?
items.e: 60 ÷ 10 = 6, so draw 6 squares. Check: 6 × 10 = 60. Drawing 60 would forget the key.

items.q: On a picture graph, each star stands for 10 votes. Fall got 45 votes. How many stars should be in the Fall row?
items.e: 45 ÷ 10 = 4 with 5 left over. 5 is half of 10, so draw 4 stars and half a star. Check: 4 × 10 + 5 = 45.
The Wed row has 4 stars and stands for 20 cups. 20 ÷ 4 = 5, so each star = 5 cups. Check: 4 × 5 = 20.

items.q: The Sunny row stands for 6 days. The key is missing. Each square should stand for how many days?
items.e: The Sunny row has 3 squares and stands for 6 days. 6 ÷ 3 = 2, so each square = 2 days. Check: 3 × 2 = 6.

items.q: The Pine row stands for 30 trees. The key is missing. Each circle should stand for how many trees?
items.e: The Pine row has 3 circles and stands for 30 trees. 30 ÷ 3 = 10, so each circle = 10 trees. Check: 3 × 10 = 30.

items.q: Maya made this bar graph from the data: Orange 4, Banana 12, Pear 10, Apple 8. Which bar is drawn wrong?
items.e: Check each bar against the data. The Orange bar ends at 2, but the data says 4. The scale counts by 2, so 4 should be 2 spaces tall, not 1 space.

items.q: Zoe made this bar graph from the data: Omar 30, Kai 35, Ruby 15, Lily 25. Which bar is drawn wrong?
items.e: Check each bar against the data. The Ruby bar ends at 20, but the data says 15. It is one line too high.

items.q: Nora made this bar graph from the data: Oak 60, Birch 50, Maple 70, Pine 20. Which bar is drawn wrong?
items.e: Check each bar against the data. The Pine bar ends at 10, but the data says 20. It is one line too low.

items.q: The four classes want to collect 200 cans in all. How many more cans do they need?
items.e: Step 1: cans so far: 40 + 25 + 55 + 30 = 150. Step 2: 200 − 150 = 50, so they need 50 more cans.

items.q: Each cup of lemonade costs $2. How much money did the stand make on Thursday and Friday together?
items.e: Step 1: cups on Thursday and Friday: 25 + 35 = 60. Step 2: each cup is $2, so 60 × 2 = $120.
Step 1: The Ava row has 3 stars and half a star: 3 × 2 = 6, and half of 2 is 1, so 6 + 1 = 7 books. Step 2: 20 − 7 = 13 more books. (Counting 4 stars as 4 books gives 16, which is wrong.)

items.q: The graph shows all 30 days of April. The class had recess outside on every day that was not rainy. On how many days did the class have recess outside?
items.e: Step 1: the Rainy bar ends at the line for 8, so 8 days were rainy. Step 2: 30 − 8 = 22 days. Check: 12 + 7 + 3 = 22.

items.q: The park plants 25 more pine trees. Then how many more pine trees than oak trees will the park have?
items.e: Step 1: pine trees after planting: 20 + 25 = 45. Step 2: compare with oak: 45 − 35 = 10 more pine trees.
